# `orbit()` {#fn-orbit}

In A08, coordinates on the two plotted solar-limit tracks recovered their source declinations by spherical inversion. [A08 results](a08-target-ranges.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-orbit)

```{=html}
<p>Latitude and declination determine where a diurnal track can meet the terrain. The
function sweeps equatorial right ascension through 360 degrees at the requested angular
step and converts each position to horizontal coordinates with the selected refraction
and atmosphere settings. It retains altitudes above -20 degrees and sorts the points by
azimuth. A horizon object supplies the location; the stored track itself includes no
test of terrain obstruction or event times.
</p>
```

**Interpretation and limits.** An orbit is sampled from an idealised fixed-declination track. A spatial equinox uses site-specific solstitial crossing geometry. State which eastern or western skyline feature supports an archaeological interpretation of the midpoint.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>dec</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Declination of object.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>loc</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Location, either a <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em> or a vector
containing the latitude and longitude of location, in this order.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>refraction</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Logical. Apply atmospheric refraction. Defaults to the session setting in <code>skyscapeR.vars</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>atm</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Atmospheric pressure in mbar. Defaults to the session setting in <code>skyscapeR.vars</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>temp</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Air temperature in degrees Celsius. Defaults to the session setting in <code>skyscapeR.vars</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>res</code></th><td><code>0.25</code></td><td><p>The resolution (in degrees of RA) with which to calculate the path.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A skyscapeR.orbit list with az and alt vectors in degrees, ordered by azimuth, plus the input declination (dec) and location (georef). The sampled track retains altitudes above -20 degrees.
</p>
```

</details>

**Implementation.** `R/mechanics.R`.
